original_question: For a one-dimensional excited random walk X = (X_n)_{n >= 0}, find conditions that force a zero-one law for the directional escape events. In other words, determine hypotheses under which each of P_0[sup_n X_n = infinity], P_0[inf_n X_n = -infinity], P_0[X_n -> infinity], and P_0[X_n -> -infinity] belongs to {0,1}.
target_in_paper: Problem 3.5 (d = 1) in Section 3.1, which asks for conditions implying zero-one laws for the one-sided escape/transience events obtained by dropping absolute values from Theorem 2.3 and Theorem 3.2. The generic priority note about “Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, Theorem 1.3” does not fit this paper’s numbering; your draft clearly matches Problem 3.5 instead. ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct dimension (d = 1), the averaged law P0, and exactly the four probabilities appearing in Problem 3.5: P0[supn Xn = +∞], P0[infn Xn = -∞], P0[Xn → +∞], and P0[Xn → -∞]. It also correctly frames the issue as a zero-one law for directional escape/transience events. ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))
missing_details: The draft does not state the precise model from Section 1: X is the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor excited random walk on Z started at 0, defined from a random cookie environment ω by the transition rule (1.1), and P0 is the averaged law obtained by integrating the quenched law over the environment measure P. ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))

The official formulation is an open-ended problem about hypotheses on the environment law P; it does not ask for a complete necessary-and-sufficient criterion, only to “find conditions which imply” the zero-one law. ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))

The provenance of the question is implicit in your draft but explicit in the paper: it arises by rephrasing the infinite-range event in Theorem 2.3 as {supn |Xn| = ∞} and then dropping absolute values there and in Theorem 3.2. ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))

The draft does not mention the paper’s explicit equivalence statement: under assumptions (SE) and (EL), the zero-one laws for the escape events (3.4) and the directional-limit events (3.5) are equivalent, using Theorems 3.2 and 2.3 together with Lemma 2.2. ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))

If the question is meant to reflect the paper’s nearby positive results, it should note that Theorem 3.10 already gives two sufficient regimes: (3.9) (SE), (POS1), and P[ω(0,1,·) = (1, 1/2, 1/2, ...)] < 1; or (3.10) (IID), (BD), and (WEL). ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))

To invoke those regimes in a fully stand-alone formulation, one must also define (POS1) for d = 1, the bounded-cookie condition (BD), weak ellipticity (WEL), and M(z), the number of non-placebo cookies at site z. ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))
refined_question: Let X = (Xn)n≥0 be the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor excited random walk on Z, started at 0 and defined under the averaged law P0 associated with a cookie-environment law P on Ω = M{-1,+1}^{Z×N} via the transition rule (1.1). Find hypotheses on the environment law P that force a directional zero-one law, namely that P0[supn≥0 Xn = +∞], P0[infn≥0 Xn = -∞] ∈ {0,1}; and, equivalently whenever P satisfies (SE) and (EL), that P0[Xn → +∞], P0[Xn → -∞] ∈ {0,1}. ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Under assumptions (SE) and (EL), this is equivalently the problem of finding conditions under which either one of the two zero-one statements in Problem 3.5 holds: (3.4) P0[supn≥0 Xn = +∞], P0[infn≥0 Xn = -∞] ∈ {0,1}, or (3.5) P0[Xn → +∞], P0[Xn → -∞] ∈ {0,1}; the paper explicitly says these are equivalent via Theorem 3.2, Theorem 2.3, and Lemma 2.2. ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Problem 3.5 because it reproduces the exact four probabilities listed there. The nearby context the paper itself uses is: Definition 3.1 for directional transience and Aℓ; Theorem 3.2 for the existing zero-one law with absolute values; Theorem 2.3 and Lemma 2.2 for the range and recurrence/transience implications; and Theorem 3.10 for two concrete sufficient hypothesis sets already known. Therefore the sharp, paper-faithful reformulation is an open problem about hypotheses on the environment law P for a one-dimensional ERW, with the escape-event and directional-limit formulations linked only under (SE) and (EL). ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))
